subject: Urban Planning
title: The Shared Street: Cars and People Together
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Shared Street: Cars and People Together usable.

hook.text: What if streets had no curbs, no lanes, and no traffic signs — and everyone just... figured it out?

buildup.text: Shared space design removes all traffic signals. Drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians negotiate in real time.

discovery.text: When drivers can't rely on signs, they slow down and make eye contact. Accidents drop dramatically.

twist.text: Blind and disabled advocates oppose shared spaces. Without curbs and signals, they can't navigate safely.

climax.text: Some cities now use hybrid designs: shared zones with tactile paving for accessibility.

punchline.text: Remove the signs and people cooperate. But not everyone can.

quiz.question: Why do shared space streets reduce accidents?
options: Fewer vehicles use the street due to inconvenience
Drivers slow down and make eye contact without signals to rely on
Pedestrians learn to avoid the street entirely
